Subject: Onboarding: private VPC bootstrap — DNS + CSR process questions

Hi Jasmine,

We’re getting our private VPC deployment scheduled for next month and the security team has a short list of questions about the DNS and certificate bootstrap flow so we can sign the onboarding checklist. TL;DR — how do you want us to provide SANs, and do you expect us to generate CSRs or will Redwood generate and send a CSR for our CA to sign?

Main asks:
- Which FQDNs need to be delegated vs. CNAMEd? (we have internal.*.acmeinc.net and a few service hostnames)
- Is ACME supported for private, or do you require an offline CSR + signed cert?
- Recommended SAN naming convention for Connector and Control Plane endpoints (we want to avoid rekey roll windows across services)
- Rotation cadence you expect on our side, and whether you accept customer-managed CA (we currently have an internal CA)

We’ve attached the acme-acmeinc-csr-request.txt with our tentative SAN list. Can we do a short sync this week to confirm?

Thanks,
Alex Turner

Subject: Re: Onboarding: private VPC bootstrap — DNS + CSR process questions

Thanks Alex — good questions. Short answers up front, then proposed plan.

Short answers:
- We prefer a delegated subdomain for control plane endpoints (e.g., redwood.acmeinc.net) and CNAMEs for connector hostnames inside your private namespace when possible.
- ACME for private namespaces varies by environment; for most VPC/on-prem installs we use an offline CSR flow. We can support ACME if you can expose an ACME challenge endpoint from the VPC during provisioning, but that’s more operational work on your side.
- SANs: please include both FQDN and Service FQDNs (connector1.acme.internal, controlplane.redwood.acmeinc.net). Avoid embedding IPs; we canonicalize to FQDNs for cert rotation.
- Rotation: we recommend 90 days for leaf certs, 365 for intermediate. Customer-managed CA is supported but we require audit of the CA's signing policy and an automated rotation procedure.

Proposed onboarding steps (30–45 minute sync + asynchronous handoff):
1) Sync call to confirm final SAN list and delegation approach (we can run the delegation verification together).
2) You either: (A) provide signed certs from your CA for the attached CSR we generate, or (B) we accept a CSR you generate and send back to you for signing.
3) Exchange DNS delegation details and test resolution in a staging VPC.
4) Smoke test TLS termination and mTLS handshake with a temporary cert before full rollout.

I’ve attached our CSR guidelines (csr-guidelines.pdf) — it includes example CN/SAN patterns and the offline CSR attributes we populate. Karhtik (cc) will drive the technical handoff; Marissa will coordinate the security checklist. Diego will help verify DNS changes in staging.

Propose Thursday 04/08 at 09:00 PDT for the call — works for you?

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.ai

On Thu, Apr 7, 2027 at 10:02 AM Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I’ve attached our CSR guidelines (csr-guidelines.pdf) — it includes example CN/SAN patterns and the offline CSR attributes we populate.

Quick technical notes from my side to make the call efficient:
- If Acme uses an internal CA, we have two supported flows:
  1) Customer-managed certs: Acme generates private key + CSR (recommended for high-security shops). We provide the CSR template and install the signed leaf cert and chain.
  2) Redwood-generated CSR: We generate a CSR (we never ship private keys), you sign and return the cert. This is useful if you want standardized CSR attributes we control.
- SAN patterns we will enforce in the runtime: controlplane.redwood.{your-domain}, *.connectors.{your-internal-domain} (wildcard allowed only one level). We cannot accept multi-level wildcards.
- DNS delegation: We prefer NS delegation of a subdomain (redwood.acmeinc.net) to reduce risk of accidental record overlap. If NS delegation is not possible, a tight TTL CNAME map for each host is acceptable.
- Testing tips: bring these test commands to the call:
  - openssl s_client -connect controlplane.redwood.acmeinc.net:443 -servername controlplane.redwood.acmeinc.net -tls1_3 -verify_return_error
  - curl --resolve 'controlplane.redwood.acmeinc.net:443:10.10.2.12' https://controlplane.redwood.acmeinc.net/healthz

I’ll prepare a short checklist for the call: final SAN list, delegation method, sample signed cert chain, and a staging DNS entry.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — short recap and agreed action items from today’s sync (we kept the call to 25 minutes):

Agreed approach:
- Acme will do customer-managed CSR flow (they will generate key + CSR). Redwood will provide the exact CSR template and attributes.
- DNS: Acme to NS-delegate redwood.acmeinc.net to the Redwood delegation name servers listed in the attachment. If legal prevents NS delegation, Acme will provide CNAME records for each connector host.
- SANs: final list confirmed in Drive (link below). Wildcard allowed for one level (*.connectors.acme.internal). No IPs in certs.
- Rotation: Acme will run a 90-day rotation for leaf certs; Redwood will notify 15 days prior to expiry for staging replacement.

Action items and owners:
- Alex (Acme): produce CSR and test cert by 2027-04-12 and upload to shared Drive. (acme-ops@acmeinc.com)
- Karthik (Redwood): provide CSR template and installation guide by EOD 2027-04-08. (karthik_iyer@redwood.ai)
- Marissa (Redwood Security): complete checklist verification and confirm acceptance criteria by 2027-04-13. (marissa_cole@redwood.ai)
- Diego (Redwood SRE): stage DNS and run TLS handshake smoke test on 2027-04-14. (diego_fernandez@redwood.ai)

If anything changes on timing, please reply-all. Otherwise I’ll mark the HubSpot deal with the onboarding milestone and track progress.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this live.

Best,
